叫.notes: Phonosemantic compound. 口 represents the meaning and 丩 represents the sound.

对.notes: Simplified form of 對. Origin unclear. Appears to be a hand using some sort of tool, possibly a rake or a hoe.

components.hint: Shorthand for the left component of 對, possibly depicting a rake or hoe.
Used here to represent a hand.

definitions: you (informal, as opposed to courteous 您[nín])
你.notes: Phonosemantic compound. 亻 represents the meaning and 尔 represents the sound.

components.hint: 亻 is a component form of 人.
The pronunciation of 你 was similar to 尔 in old Chinese, but they no longer sound similar in modern Mandarin due to historical phonetic changes. 尔 also serves as a meaning component.

好.notes: It is good (好) for a woman (女) and her child (子) to be together.

我.notes: Pictograph of a weapon or farming tool with a forked blade and long handle. The meaning "I; me" is a phonetic loan.

definitions: prefix used before the surname of a person or a numeral indicating the order of birth of the children in a family or to indicate affection or familiarity
老.notes: Pictograph of an old person with long hair bent over and leaning on a cane.

components.hint: Depicts an old man bent over.

师.notes: Simplified form of 師.  Origin unclear.

components.hint: Shorthand for the 𠂤 component in the traditional character 師. The purpose of this component is unclear.
The purpose of this component is unclear.

学.notes:
Simplified form of 學.  Originally composed of the numbers five (㐅) and six (六), representing study of arithmetic. 
Later two hands (又) were added on the left and right side of the character, possibly depicting counting with fingers or hands-on teaching.
Finally a child (子) was added to the bottom, depicting a child being educated.
The bottom part of 六 (six) was reanalyzed as 宀 (roof) and interpreted as a building for learning.

components.hint: Shorthand form of the 㐅 (five), 六 (six), and 又 (hand) components in the top part of the traditional character 學.

生.notes: Pictograph of a sprout emerging from the ground.

definitions: (of clothes) classifier for number of washes

瓶.notes: Phonosemantic compound. 瓦 represents the meaning and 并 represents the sound. Simplified form of 缾.

definitions: also pr. [yāo] for greater clarity when spelling out numbers digit by digit
一.notes: A single horizontal stroke, representing the number one.

咖.notes: Phonosemantic compound. 口 represents the meaning and 加 represents the sound.

啡.notes: Phonosemantic compound. 口 represents the meaning and 非 represents the sound.

definitions: classifier for things with mouths (people, domestic animals, cannons, wells etc)

丩.notes: Pictograph of two ropes entangled together, now written as 糾.

又.notes: Pictograph of a hand. The character is based on the original meaning "right hand", which is unrelated to the modern meaning.

寸.notes: Pictograph of a hand with a line marking a spot on the wrist. In traditional Chinese medicine this spot on the wrist where the pulse can be taken is called the 寸口.

亻.notes: 亻 is a component form of 人.

尔.notes: Simplified form of 爾.  Origin unclear. Used in ancient texts to mean "you".

女.notes: Pictograph of a woman. Depicts a stick-figure with breasts sitting or squatting down.

子.notes: Pictograph of a small child with its two arms outstretched.

戈.notes: Pictograph of a weapon with a long shaft and horizontal blade.

瓦.notes: Pictograph of a tool for making pottery.

并.notes: Simplified form of 並.  Depits two people standing (立) side-by-side.

definitions: (used after an adverb such as 不, 大, 稍 etc, and before a disyllabic verb, to indicate that the action of the verb is applied to sth or sb previously mentioned)
加.notes: Depicts making noises with the mouth (口) while exerting strength (力). Based on the original meaning "exert strength". The meaning later shifted to "raise; increase; add"

非.notes: Pictograph of two wings facing opposite directions.

立.notes: Pictograph of a person standing on the ground.

力.notes: Pictograph of a plow, representing strength
